design.behavior: Initialize an enabled progress record for every skill in skills. On each timer tick, append the existing stage verification line followed by one selected-skill progress line containing the skill name, stage context, and deterministic count/percentage. Advance the shared stage cursor once. On completion, retain the active skill's complete state and append the existing checkpoint once; inactive skills remain explicitly tracked at their current value.
design.state: Keep selected, running, stage, and trace in src/routes/index.tsx; derive a per-skill progress map from skills, derive selectedSkill from harnesses[selected], and reset the map deterministically per run without persistence or a global store.
design.presentation: Keep the five-stage strip intact and add per-skill progress metadata to every homepage skill card plus a clearly labeled active-skill progress panel in the trace card. Show each skill's enabled state and count/percentage, with 0/10 through 10/10 for the active run. Use semantic text and restrained visual fill; retain aria-live for meaningful trace updates.
notChanged: src/content.ts unless a display label or stable progress constant cannot be derived from existing skill data

risks: Per-skill state could omit a catalog entry or accidentally share progress between skills.
Paired events could accidentally advance the stage twice or duplicate the completion checkpoint.
A derived skill label could become stale after scenario switching.
Ten trace events may increase live-region verbosity.
mitigations: Initialize from the skills array and inspect all 14 ids in the transcript.
Advance the existing cursor once per timer tick and assert exact transcript ordering.
Reset trace/progress on scenario selection and derive the label from selected index.
Use concise event text and keep the existing single aria-live region.
risksAndRecovery.rollback: Remove the new skill event/state and presentation while retaining the original stage effect and strip; no persisted data or migration exists.
risksAndRecovery.forwardRecovery: If visual density is too high, preserve the event contract and reduce decorative UI while keeping the textual count and selected skill visible.

critiqueResolution.finding: The plan must preserve existing stage progress rather than replace it.
